not sure if this is helping anyhow but I have noticed that when I create a new project with Forward+ in 4.6.2 it adds
```
[rendering]

rendering_device/driver.windows="d3d12"
renderer/rendering_method="forward_plus"
```
to project.godot and it crashes at launch as expected.
If I now remove that part and launch again, it works perfectly fine and still shows Forward+ as selected rendering engine in the Editor GUI.

When running the project, it shows

```
Godot Engine v4.6.2.stable.official.71f334935 - https://godotengine.org
Vulkan 1.4.323 - Forward+ - Using Device #0: Intel - Intel(R) Iris(R) Xe Graphics
```

So I guess its working now because it uses Vulkan and not D3D?

Inital testing with updated Nvidia GPU driver, (610.47 > 595.71), appears stable.

Project frozen using **_Vulkan_** drivers. No errors or logs. Restart required.
I will continue working with D3D12 and will report any issues.

`Godot v4.7.beta5 - Windows 11 (build 26200) - Multi-window, 2 monitors - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA RTX A500 Laptop GPU (NVIDIA; 32.0.16.1047) - 13th Gen Intel(R) Core(TM) i7-13700H (20 threads) - 31.68 GiB memory - WASAPI (48000 Hz, Stereo/mono)`

I received the following 'errors' while playtesting with D3D12 drivers:

```
ERROR: Cannot create uniform set because there's not enough room in the RESOURCES descriptor heap.
Please increase the value of the rendering/rendering_device/d3d12/max_resource_descriptors project setting.
   at: uniform_set_create (drivers/d3d12/rendering_device_driver_d3d12.cpp:3387)
ERROR: Condition "!driver_uniform_set" is true. Returning: RID()
   at: uniform_set_create (servers/rendering/rendering_device.cpp:4767)
ERROR: Parameter "uniform_set" is null.
   at: compute_list_bind_uniform_set (servers/rendering/rendering_device.cpp:6750)
ERROR: Uniforms were never supplied for set (2) at the time of drawing, which are required by the pipeline.
   at: compute_list_dispatch (servers/rendering/rendering_device.cpp:6839)

```

Doubling the d3d12 values, as per the very informative error messages, appears to have corrected the problem.
```
Project Settings > Rendering > Rendering Device > D3D12 > Max Resource Descriptors : 131072  (was 65536)
Project Settings > Rendering > Rendering Device > D3D12 > Max Sampler Descriptors : 2048  (was 1024)
```

With a similar hope to alleviate issues with the Vulkan driver, I have quadrupled the Vulkan Max Descriptors per Pool:
`Project Settings > Rendering > Rendering Device > Vulkan > Max Descriptors per Pool : 256  (was 64)`

Initial testing of Vulkan drivers is lasting longer during playtests with no freezes as yet.
